correctness.rationale: Grange's stationary flux equations and matching yield F=v rho/v_0, F'=-chi rho on x>0, F(0)=c, F(b)=1, with the selected low-density root on the gas side and b=log(c)/(mu chi)>0. The normalization is exact: integrating the flux slope with F(infinity)=0 gives mass c/chi per side. The flux itself gives a direct independent moment computation: P(|X|>x)=F(x)/c. In the tail integral for E|X|, change variable from x to z=F(x); the integrand after factoring out 1/(c chi) is z/rho(z). In the core rho=mu z, so the integral from z=1 to c is (c-1)/mu. In the gas z/rho(z)=(1+sqrt(1-4z/mu))/2, positive and bounded on [0,1], with the continuous limit at zero. Its integral is 1/2+(mu/12)[1-(1-4/mu)^(3/2)], equal to (1+q+4/q)/6 using mu=q^2/(q-1), q in (1,2). Differentiating gives dE|X|/dmu=[q(q+2)/6-(c-1)]/(c chi mu^2). Since q strictly decreases, q(q+2)/6 falls strictly from 4/3 to 1/2. This gives strict monotonicity even at c=3/2 and 7/3 (the endpoints are excluded), and a unique maximum with q_*=-1+sqrt(6c-5) otherwise. Using (c-1)=q_*(q_*+2)/6 in the moment gives the claimed height; q=2 and 1 give both endpoint limits. The half-width decreases directly at fixed c,chi. Independent flux-coordinate quadrature at 90 settings agreed to absolute error below 6.2e-10; the analytic derivative, not the grid, proves the classification.
residual_risks: The proof follows the specified matched stationary branch. It does not show that time evolution selects it or that it is dynamically stable, and the endpoint values are limits only.

value.rationale: The normalized mean distance is a whole-distribution localization statistic, whereas the known shrinking core describes only one boundary. The core mass remains fixed as crowding changes, yet the increasing, peaked and decreasing global response regimes differ. The exact parameter cutoffs and peak location identify when the core width is a misleading proxy for spread. This is a complete parameter response across a natural branch, not a numerical counterexample or an isolated integral.
residual_risks: Scientific value here is a stationary continuum comparison; it does not predict nonequilibrium behavior beyond the model.
